_meta.notes: SHA governs inter-se rights of shareholders. Must be mirrored in AOA to be enforceable against company - V.B. Rangaraj v. V.B. Gopalakrishnan (1992) 1 SCC 160. SEBI ICDR Regulations may apply for listed entities.

title: Shareholders Agreement (SHA)

dispute_resolution.default: Arbitration under Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996

mandatory_clauses.title: Representations and Warranties (by Company and Founders)
Reserved Matters / Affirmative Vote Items
mandatory_clauses.note: Must be mirrored in AOA to bind company - V.B. Rangaraj

mandatory_clauses.title: Right of First Refusal / Right of First Offer
Tag-Along Rights
mandatory_clauses.content: If a Founder proposes to transfer shares constituting >= {{tag_along_threshold}}% of share capital, the Investor shall have the right to participate in such sale pro rata.

mandatory_clauses.title: Drag-Along Rights
mandatory_clauses.content: If shareholders holding >= {{drag_along_threshold}}% approve a sale, remaining shareholders shall be required to sell on the same terms.

mandatory_clauses.title: Exit Rights (IPO, Strategic Sale, Buyback, Put Option)
mandatory_clauses.note: Put options on Indian residents by non-residents face FEMA constraints - structure carefully

mandatory_clauses.title: Founder Non-Compete and Non-Solicit
mandatory_clauses.note: Post-employment non-compete on founders qua employees void under S.27 Contract Act; non-compete qua shareholders enforceable - Niranjan Shankar Golikari

mandatory_clauses.title: Governing Law and Dispute Resolution
mandatory_clauses.content: This Agreement is governed by the laws of India. Disputes shall be referred to arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 seated at {{arbitration_seat}}.

mandatory_clauses.title: Amendment of AOA to Reflect SHA
Miscellaneous (Notices, Severability, Entire Agreement, Force Majeure)

prompt_context.system_role: You are drafting a Shareholders Agreement for an Indian private limited company. Balance founder protection and investor rights. Ensure SHA terms are mirrorable in AOA (V.B. Rangaraj). Comply with FEMA if foreign investor.
drafting_rules: Identify parties clearly - Founders, Investors, Company, ESOP Trust.
Reserved matters list should be specific (e.g., charter amendments, M&A, debt above threshold, related party transactions, business plan changes, key hires).
Tag-along triggers on Founder exit; Drag-along requires defined threshold.
ROFR vs ROFO - distinguish clearly. ROFR = existing holder matches third-party offer; ROFO = existing holder gets first offer.
Anti-dilution: broad-based weighted average is most founder-friendly. Full ratchet most investor-friendly.
Liquidation preference - default 1x non-participating to align incentives.
Founder vesting/reverse vesting: 4 years, 1-year cliff is market standard.
Non-compete on founder qua shareholder is enforceable; qua employee post-termination void under S.27.
Put option on Indian resident by foreign investor - structure as exit assistance, not assured return (FEMA).
Stamp duty payable per state Stamp Act (avg INR 100-500 plus value-linked in some states).
Arbitration seat usually Mumbai/Delhi/Bengaluru - mention venue and seat both.
prompt_context.tone: Formal commercial-legal, US-style VC document conventions adapted for Indian law.

filing_checklist: Stamp the agreement per state stamp duty (e.g., Maharashtra: 0.2% of consideration; Delhi: INR 100; Karnataka: 0.1%).
Amend AOA to reflect SHA clauses (esp. transfer restrictions, board nomination, affirmative vote) - file MGT-14.
If foreign investor: file FC-GPR within 30 days of share allotment (RBI).
Issue share certificates within 2 months of allotment (S.56 Cos Act).
Update ROM (Register of Members) under S.88.
PAS-3 filing for return of allotment within 15 days.

validation_rules.rule: All material SHA clauses mirrored in AOA
validation_rules.check: Transfer restrictions, board, affirmative vote in AOA
If any party non-resident, FC-GPR/FC-TRS mentioned
